knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.2.8
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) What is the bootstrap method move for obtaining a confidence interval? (2) What is resampled? (3) Name one reason this is not the same as finishing hypothesis testing (3.3).
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Resample from the sample (or an appropriate bootstrap mechanism under CMP), form the interval statistic on replicates, and obtain a bootstrap confidence interval. Hypothesis testing is topic 3.3 — not today's LO.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.2.8
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) Outline the bootstrap move to obtain a confidence interval for a parameter (percentile idea is enough). (2) Refuse: 'Bootstrap for an estimator standard error is the same as a bootstrap confidence interval' and 'finishing a bootstrap CI finishes hypothesis testing.'
knowledge_checks.body: Bootstrap CI procedure; refuse properties-bootstrap-as-CI and HT-as-done.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Bootstrap CIs use the replicate distribution to form interval endpoints; that differs from SE-only bootstrap and from HT.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) Resample with replacement, recompute the statistic on each resample, then form an interval from the bootstrap distribution of that statistic (e.g. percentile interval from the α/2 and 1−α/2 quantiles of the replicates). (2) Refuse: estimating an estimator property is not the same as constructing a CI; hypothesis testing is a different LO.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Equating bootstrap estimator-property estimation with bootstrap CI construction, or claiming HT is finished.
success_criteria: Outlines resample → replicate statistic → interval from bootstrap distribution.
Refuses conflating with bootstrap SE estimation or hypothesis testing.
